report.summary: Chunk 10 of 11 of parse.py: implements _annassign, _assign, _visit, _pep695_alias, and facts; handles type aliases, field declarations, and PEP 695.
risks: _assign | low | NewType detection uses _dotted_tail on node.value.func but does not check that node.value.func is a Name or Attribute; could raise AttributeError on malformed call. | Verify that _dotted_tail handles all possible AST node types for func.
_assign | medium | When NewType has no args, alias_target is set to annotation_text(None) which may produce unexpected results. | Check annotation_text behaviour with None.
_visit | low | The recursion depth limit _STMT_DEPTH is not defined in this chunk; if it is missing or misconfigured, truncated may never be set. | Ensure _STMT_DEPTH is defined in module scope.
facts | low | Sorting keys use t.line, t.qualname, t.kind; if line is None for some types, sorting may raise TypeError. | Confirm that all TypeDecls have a valid line number.

handoff.purpose: Define visitor methods for annotated assignments, plain assignments, general descent, PEP 695 type aliases, and the facts() method.

symbols.name: _annassign
symbols.note: Handles AnnAssign nodes; creates TypeDecl for TypeAlias, FieldDecl for class members, and FieldDecl for self assignments.

symbols.name: _assign
symbols.note: Handles Assign nodes; creates TypeDecl for NewType calls, FieldDecl for class members and self assignments.

symbols.name: _visit
symbols.note: Recursively visits child nodes dispatching to specialized handlers; tracks depth and sets truncated if exceeded.

symbols.name: _pep695_alias
symbols.note: Creates TypeDecl for PEP 695 type alias nodes (Python 3.12+).

symbols.name: facts
symbols.note: Returns a PyTypeFacts tuple with sorted types, fields, and signatures.

claims.text: ``Vec: TypeAlias = list[int]`` declares a type, not a member.
claims.why: The code checks tail == 'TypeAlias' and target is ast.Name, then appends a TypeDecl and returns, avoiding field creation.

claims.text: ``X = NewType("X", int)`` is the one unannotated assignment that unambiguously declares a type.
claims.why: The code specifically checks for ast.Call with _dotted_tail == 'NewType' and single Name target, then creates a TypeDecl.

claims.text: A bare ``X = int`` is NOT treated as an alias: at module level that shape is far more often a constant, and minting a type node for it would fabricate declarations.
claims.why: The code only creates TypeDecl for NewType calls; a plain assignment like X = int goes to the general assignment handling, which does not create a TypeDecl.

claims.text: Sored, not merely "whatever the descent produced". The descent IS deterministic, but two processes must agree byte-for-byte and a sort makes that true by construction rather than by argument.
claims.why: The facts() method returns sorted tuples using key=lambda t: (t.line, t.qualname, t.kind) for types and similar for fields and signatures.

observations.what: In _annassign, when tail == 'TypeAlias', annotation_text is called on node.value, but the comment says 'alias_target=annotation_text(node.value)'. The variable 'annotation' is not used in that branch.
In _assign, the NewType detection does not verify that node.value.func is either ast.Name or ast.Attribute; _dotted_tail may fail on other node types.
In _assign, when NewType has less than 2 args, arg becomes None and annotation_text(None) is called; behaviour unknown.

In _visit, the variable alias_node is assigned getattr(ast, 'TypeAlias', None) and used in isinstance check; if ast.TypeAlias does not exist, alias_node is None and isinstance(child, None) returns False, so PEP 695 aliases are silently ignored.
The facts() method sorts types by (t.line, t.qualname, t.kind). If t.line is None, sorting will raise TypeError.
The facts() method returns PyTypeFacts with fields from self.fields and signatures from self.signatures, but self.signatures is not defined in this chunk; it may be defined elsewhere or missing.
